arguments.name: Alexander’s brain-independence argument
arguments.position: Strongest conditional reconstruction, not endorsed conclusion
premises: If relevant brain processes were excluded during that experience, a specified ordinary production account would fail.
Claimed external details and prior description might strengthen accuracy if independently verified.
bridge_principles: Retrospective memory accurately dates its content to the excluded interval.
Clinical evidence rules out all processes required by the targeted model.
Alternate ordinary information routes do not explain verified details.
arguments.conclusion: Conditional support for H-B; no automatic H-S/H-T or deity inference
arguments.strongest_objection: A-T06-002: neither temporal alignment nor exclusion of all relevant processing is established.
arguments.strongest_reply: Defender appeals to profound impairment, different recovery phenomenology and corroborative detail rather than credentials alone.
unresolved_issues: Recoverable brain illness is not irreversible death.
Even H-B needs a substrate definition; other physical realization is logically possible.

arguments.name: Underdetermination and ordinary alternatives
arguments.position: Audit reconstruction with Shermer’s original challenge
premises: Reports and clinical severity do not directly identify the moment each memory formed.
A feeling of reality alone cannot validate external objects.
Ordinary mechanisms may remain possible without any one being demonstrated.
bridge_principles: A claim that excludes a mechanism must establish the relevant exclusion, not rely solely on explanatory incompleteness.
arguments.conclusion: This packet does not identify a unique neural or non-neural cause
arguments.strongest_objection: A-T06-001: severe impairment and corroborated details could challenge a precisely specified brain-dependent account.
arguments.strongest_reply: Preserve corroborative reports and propose independently dated/timed tests; do not declare hallucination merely because it is possible.
unresolved_issues: Raw records and prospective synchronization absent.
Comparator studies and direct Sacks source not inspected.

arguments.name: Severe illness versus solely pharmacological coma
premises: Clinical review attributes pre-sedation deterioration to illness while acknowledging mixed later contributions.
bridge_principles: Different descriptions can concern different stages and mechanisms; quotations alone do not settle physiology.
arguments.conclusion: Avoid both drug-only dismissal and inference from serious illness to complete brain inactivity
arguments.strongest_objection: Witness accounts are retrospective and contested.
arguments.strongest_reply: Published chart review strengthens severe-illness documentation but is not a continuous functional recording.
unresolved_issues: Original interview and clinical chronology needed to settle remaining particulars.
